clue.text: Quiet increasingly embarrassed evidence destroyer?

parts.note: SH is the hushing call asking for quiet
someone more embarrassed is redder in the face

explanation.surface: A hushed figure blushing ever deeper suggests someone caught with incriminating papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: a machine that shreds papers can dispose of incriminating documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper-cutting machine is what an office uses to get rid of incriminating documents, so it destroys evidence.

clue.text: Artist of very fashionable merit

parts.note: hep is an old form of hip, meaning very fashionable
worth means merit or value

explanation.surface: Praise for a painter whose work is both stylish and worthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Hepworth was a celebrated British sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Trade in obsolete coins?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
loose coins are called change

explanation.surface: Dealing in coins that are no longer legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade or swap one thing for another is to make an exchange.

clue.text: Downfall of party over ending of Thatcherism

parts.note: a do is a party
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: ending of picks the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The collapse of a political party once the Thatcher era ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom means ruin or a terrible fate, the same as a fall from power.

clue.text: Parrot sprang completely upwards

parts.note: rose means sprang up

indicators.note: in a down entry, upwards means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: A parrot leapt straight up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upwards' signals writing bottom to top; the rosella is native to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosella is a brightly coloured Australian parrot.

clue.text: Son gets upset belly with fruit when it's past its best?

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: A boy gets a stomach upset from eating fruit that had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges BELLY to ELLBY; it suits the surface's tummy trouble too.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed limit on food packaging marks the point after which the product should no longer be sold.

clue.text: Gun with zero plastic

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: A gun made with no plastic at all, or a plastic gun scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' rearranges WITH ZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece firing shells at a high angle.

clue.text: Boring group made to assemble at home

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
a pack is a group, as of wolves

explanation.surface: A dull bunch forced to gather at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture sold in boxed pieces is designed for the buyer to put together themselves.

clue.text: Chill excessively, remaining calm

parts.note: over means left or remaining, as in food left over
cool means calm and unflustered

explanation.surface: Advice to someone staying composed while overdoing the refrigeration.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something too cold is to chill it more than needed, a compound of over- and cool.

clue.text: Superficially misleading issue cop sorted out

indicators.note: letters sorted out are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A deceptive matter that a police officer has dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges the letters of ISSUE COP.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that seems plausible on the surface but is actually false is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Lie with gusto outrageously? One might

definitions.text: Lie with gusto outrageously? One might

indicators.note: behaving outrageously suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who heaps extravagant praise may well stretch the truth enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges LIE GUSTO; read whole, the clue describes a praise-giver at a funeral who might exaggerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker delivering a eulogy praises the dead, often with flattering exaggeration.

clue.text: Calmly put new pen in carrier

indicators.note: put begins the instruction placing pieces in the container
in tells us the pieces go inside the container word

parts.note: a tray is something used to carry things
a quill is an old-fashioned feather pen

explanation.surface: An instruction to place a fresh pen in a holder without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in' signals the insertion; 'carrier' is a tray, not a person or vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe acting in a peaceful, untroubled manner, so they are synonymous adverbs.

clue.text: University representative broadcast in sound

parts.note: an MP, a Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
aired means broadcast

explanation.surface: A university spokesman's words went out over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests noise, but it means healthy and whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of healthy and undamaged means without any damage or weakness.

clue.text: Book unknown during long period of history

indicators.note: during means within, so the letter sits inside the period

parts.note: an era is a long period of history
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A history book with a gap in its knowledge of some epoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, so it is one example of a book.

clue.text: Supposed bird's denying exclamation after hours in Poe

indicators.note: after puts the exclamation following the rest
in places the abbreviation inside the poet's name

parts.note: nix is a slang exclamation meaning no

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe's famous bird, here given a late-night 'no!'
explanation.walkthrough: Poe wrote 'The Raven', which lures you toward ravens, but the bird is a mythical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is a legendary bird reborn from its ashes; it exists only in myth, so it is merely supposed.

clue.text: One unhappy to be kept inside light fence

indicators.note: kept inside means placed within the following word

parts.note: pale means light in colour
I is the Roman numeral one
sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: A miserable person confined behind a flimsy barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed stakes, used as a defensive enclosure.

clue.text: Female in metallic fabric, but not good for ex?

indicators.note: but not means the following letter is taken away
in places the abbreviation inside the two-word fabric

parts.note: gold lamé is a fabric woven with metallic gold threads

explanation.surface: A woman in shiny gold cloth, no longer good enough for a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes between GOLD and LAME, then 'but not' removes G.
explanation.definitionFit: A former lover or partner is often called this; the question mark covers the abbreviated form of former partner.

clue.text: Biologist's need to include sheep that's brought back

definitions.note: read as 'biologist is', the apostrophe-s linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: to include means the following piece goes inside

parts.note: lack means need or want

indicators.note: brought back signals the word for the sheep is written backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A scientist needing to contain a sheep that has been returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's brought back' signals the reversal and 'to include' the insertion; the 's of Biologist's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French naturalist known for an early theory of evolution.

clue.text: Faust Brian put together without leading notes, like Berg?

indicators.note: the first letters of each name are F and B, both musical notes, and they are dropped
put together means the two names are joined into one string

explanation.surface: Composing a Faust opera with someone named Brian, in the style of a modernist composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg was a Viennese composer; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg came from Vienna, so he was a native of that central European country.

clue.text: Cat spoiled with bream and seafood

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pampered cat fed on fish and shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges CAT and BREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of crabs is eaten as shellfish, a kind of seafood.

clue.text: What will encourage change for litmus? Iodine

indicators.note: change for means the letters are altered into another order

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab question: what makes litmus change, and does iodine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'change for' rearranges LITMUS to STIMUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural incentives or spurs to action prompt a response, so they encourage.

clue.text: Some crocodiles over in pool

indicators.note: over signals the letters are read the other way round
some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A few crocodiles are lurking in the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ODIL from crocodiles; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: The Three Broomsticks pub in Hertfordshire town

definitions.meaning: the Three Broomsticks is a pub in the Harry Potter books, so it is the answer
a commuter town north of London in the county of Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: Locating a fictional wizarding pub in a real English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is a county just north of London; the Three Broomsticks pub appears in J K Rowling's Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as a possessive, the town's name describes a drinking place belonging to the boy wizard.

clue.text: Charlie's married after single mistake

indicators.note: after places the married parts following the single one

parts.note: sole means single or only
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
the apostrophe-s of Charlie's is read as is

explanation.surface: Charlie wed after being single, which turned out to be an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, a kind of error.

clue.text: Complain when Poe's end's lost literary raven

indicators.note: lost means the letter is taken away

parts.note: gripe means complain

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Grumbling that Poe's ending lost its famous raven.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe suggests his poem 'The Raven', but the raven is Dickens's: Grip in Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge, the Dickens character, keeps a talking pet bird of this name.

clue.text: Picked up uniform getting highly promoted?

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet
to promote something highly is to praise it

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform is lifted up the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'highly promoted' as a loose, punning way of saying praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifted upward has been raised, as a hand or a flag might be.

clue.text: What helps one work out the tongue-tied Bronte?

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
the Bronte sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell

explanation.surface: Which silent Bronte sister can help you puzzle things out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like solving a problem but means exercise; the Brontes used the pen-surname Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bar with weights on each end is used for exercise in the gym.

clue.text: Current PM returned agreement for freedom

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: returned means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: unity means agreement or harmony

explanation.surface: The sitting prime minister brought back a pact securing liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PM into MP; 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from punishment, a freedom from consequences.
